one_liner: Header-only C++20 thread pool with Chase-Lev fork-join and sub-microsecond parallelFor; tops oneTBB and Taskflow on recursive fork-join.
what_it_does: citor gives one ThreadPool type with synchronous primitives: parallelFor, parallelReduce (deterministic, optional Kahan), parallelScan/inclusiveScan, parallelChain (multi-stage pipeline), runPlex (persistent workers across phases), bulkForQueries, forkJoin (recursive divide-and-conquer) and submitDetached. The calling thread participates as slot 0, bodies are passed as non-owning 16-byte FunctionRefs, and each call is templated on a compile-time Hints type (balance, determinism, affinity, priority, inline-fallback cost gates). It is not a drop-in for oneTBB/Taskflow/OpenMP APIs; code must be ported to its call shapes.
how_it_is_fast: forkJoin uses per-worker Chase-Lev work-stealing deques (Le et al. 2013 memory orderings) in the Cilk-5 spawn-parent shape: children go on the calling worker's own deque, the last child runs inline, and the join is a per-frame pendingTasks counter, with steals biased to same-CCD victims. Fan-out dispatch puts the job descriptor on the producer's stack with no hot-path allocation, joins through per-slot done-epoch barriers, parks workers with raw futexes, and pins one worker per physical core using a sysfs topology probe. Small calls fall back to running inline on the caller with no wake-up.
when_to_use: Recursive fork-join (fib, skynet, cilksort, Strassen, BVH builds) on Linux x86-64, where it had the best mean ratio (1.06x to best) in tzcnt/runtime-benchmarks on a 64-core EPYC 7742.
Latency-sensitive loops with many short parallel regions, where sub-microsecond empty fan-out and runPlex's spin rendezvous between phases cut per-dispatch overhead.
Reductions that must be bit-identical across worker counts (FixedBlockOrder or KahanCompensated determinism).
Single-CCD AMD Zen 4/Zen 5 desktops and workstations with workers pinned inside one shared L3, the stated design target.
Projects that want a header-only dependency (single_include/citor.hpp, pthread only) instead of linking oneTBB or an OpenMP runtime.
when_not_to_use: Barrier-bound stencils on multi-CCD AMD or Intel mesh servers: the README says these lose to OpenMP because the producer's done-epoch scan is linear in participant count.
Heavy-tailed reductions: parallelReduce is statically partitioned with no stealing after local completion, so oneTBB's auto_partitioner wins.
Memory-tight runs: peak RSS in runtime-benchmarks was 44.5 MB on fib(39) vs 11.69 MB for tbb and 51.01 MB vs 10.51 MB for libfork on nqueens.
nqueens- or matmul-like fork-join on many cores, where libfork and TooManyCooks were faster (nqueens 80765 us vs 69010 us; matmul(2048) 48069 us vs 44140 us).
I/O-bound or blocking task bodies, async futures, or non-x86 targets: it is a CPU-bound synchronous engine and only Linux and Windows x86-64 are validated.

integration.dependencies: none beyond pthread (Threads::Threads); MSVC needs Synchronization.lib
integration.min_toolchain: C++20; CI uses GCC 14, Clang 19 (Clang 18 for sanitizer jobs), MSVC 2022
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 (latency contract validated), Windows x86-64 (builds and tests, latency not validated); non-x86 compiles with Deadline disabled
integration.thread_safety: Concurrent producers on one pool are safe and serialize through a dispatch lease; nested same-pool parallelFor/forkJoin run in parallel, other nested primitives run inline on the caller.

gotchas: ThreadPool(n) counts the calling thread, clamps to physical cores and the affinity mask, and auto-pins the producer on Linux; check pool.participants() for the real count.
Bodies are captured by a non-owning FunctionRef, so callables must outlive the call; the pool is non-copyable and non-movable.
The Chase-Lev deque keeps every superseded ring buffer until the deque is destroyed, which is one source of the higher peak RSS.
Open issue #1: the header declares a member named slots, which breaks compilation when Qt's slots macro is in scope; submitDetached spawns a new std::thread per call.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick citor over Fork Union when you need recursive work stealing, deterministic reductions or scans in addition to fast parallel-for dispatch; pick it over Taskflow or Nowa-style runtimes when fork-join throughput matters, since it beat Taskflow by 3-7x on skynet and fib(39) in an outside suite.
verified_claims_summary: In tzcnt/runtime-benchmarks (Clang 21.1.7 -O3 -march=native, tcmalloc, EPYC 7742 with 64 threads and no SMT, boost on, schedutil), citor's mean ratio to the best runtime was 1.06x vs libfork 1.18x, TooManyCooks 1.32x, tbb 3.25x and taskflow 3.34x; skynet took 24932 us vs tbb 142887 us, and fib(39) took 49966 us vs tbb 215592 us and taskflow 156590 us. The suite's citor adapter is a straight port of the libfork fib/skynet code and pins citor v0.4.5 by default, while the current release is 0.6.2; citor's own Zen 5 sweep is published only as charts.
status_note: Actively developed (v0.6.2, last commit 2026-10-05, pre-1.0 with a stable public surface), MIT, header-only and easy to vendor; 54 stars, so production use outside the author is not documented.
